questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was generally interested in Italian cultures and particularly the political and cultural landscape present in Bologna

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some of the information was pretty easy to find, some was pretty hard. The structure of University of Bologna differs in many ways from the structure found at University of Copenhagen, which made finding information have quite a steep learning curve. But once I got hold of it, it wasn't a problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and bumped in to someone who knew a guy, but I would say that it isn't very transparent in general with regards to where you can find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, so stick to a strict budget if you don't want to end up eating nothing but porridge for the last month

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was unintuitive at best. It was not clear what the actual subjects entailed and the timetables changed last minute. This meant it was really hard to count on any of the plans that you had put out for yourself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Almost none, you could write the professors and hope that they would reply. Otherwise you could facetime a employee of the helpdesk, but it was not always helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 8 out of 10 I would say. But a lot of work went into it. And mid-term I realised that two of my classes were the same class. Long story short, I needed to figure out how to enrol in a new class last minute.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience, it's a chore

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were varying a lot. But generally there were a lot of reading and the amount of work expected exceeded the ects provided for each courses. But with a bit of planning it wasn't a big deal.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: This was varying a lot from teacher to teacher

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Italian Pop Culture, Semiotics of Conflict, Gender Studies, Women's movements worldwide, and Language and late capitalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both Semiotics of Conflict, and Language and Late Capitalism had a very exciting curriculum and really good teachers!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy if you are open minded. People are very kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take it slow and enjoy. Besides, no matter what people tell you, it's okay to buy cappuccino after 12 o'clock.
